packet.title: Invisible XML for large inputs (book, tests, implementation)

body.p: After (7.21: about 3 to 6 MB/s and linear, but 80 to 200 bytes of memory for each input character). The owner: usable on tens to hundreds of MB; the book, the tests, then the implementation; one parser ().

item.p: Done when: the book's performance chapter states the targets and passes (run-ixml-bench.py --check, with the 100 MB log under --large, and its examples); regular nonterminals compiled once into automata, ambiguity kept; memory bounded; no iXML suite or QT4 iXML case lost; , allocator memory, honest steps, no header change. Done 2026-10-20 (): regular tokens with path-counting automata, sparse item sets over UTF-8 byte positions, a parse tree without hidden nodes and with text runs. Log 1 MB 0.20 s / 90 MB to 0.06 s / 21 MB (84 to 10 MB per further MB); 10 MB 2.0 s / 831 MB to 0.6 s / 124 MB; 100 MB 6.2 s / 1.17 GB within the default step limit; suite 886/907 and QT4 fn-invisible-xml 16/16 unchanged.
